p.src: We shall say no more for now of how the four pilgrims escaped and rose upon the wind with the Vajra Guardians. Instead, we tell how the many people at the Life-Saving Temple in Chen Family Village rose at daybreak and again prepared fruit and delicacies as offerings, only to reach the foot of the tower and find the Tang Monk gone. One asked here and another searched there; all were flustered and at a loss, lamenting bitterly, “We let a living Buddha slip away before our very eyes!” Having no remedy for the moment, they carried all the prepared offerings upstairs, performed rites, and burned paper offerings. Thereafter they held four great sacrifices and twenty-four lesser ones every year. Those praying for recovery from illness or for safety, those seeking marriages and making vows, and those asking for wealth or children came at all hours and on every day to burn incense and give thanks. Truly, the golden brazier’s fire burned unbroken for a thousand years, and the jade lamp shone forever through ten thousand ages. But we shall speak no more of this.

p.src: The Eight Vajra Guardians then raised a second fragrant wind and, in less than a day, carried the four pilgrims to the Eastern Land, where Chang’an gradually came into view. It happened that Emperor Taizong, having escorted the Tang Monk out of the city three days before the full moon of the ninth month in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, ordered officials of the Ministry of Works in the sixteenth year to build a Scripture-Watching Tower beyond the Xi’an Pass, from which to welcome the scriptures. Every year Taizong visited the place in person. On that very day he had again driven out to the tower, when suddenly he saw the western sky filled with auspicious vapors and waves of fragrant wind. The Guardians halted in midair and called, “Holy Monk, the city below is Chang’an. We had better not descend: the people here are sharp-eyed, and our forms might be revealed. Nor need the Great Sage Sun and the other two go. Go alone and deliver the scriptures to your sovereign, then return at once. We shall wait for you in the heavens and go with you to report the fulfillment of our charge.” The Great Sage said, “Your words are reasonable, Venerable Ones, but how could our master carry the scripture bundles? And how could he lead this horse? We must accompany him to see him safely there. Please wait a little while in the sky; we surely will not delay.” The Guardians said, “The other day Bodhisattva Guanyin informed the Tathagata that the round trip must take only eight days, thereby completing the prescribed number of days for the canon. More than four days have already passed. We fear Bajie may covet wealth and honor and make us miss the deadline.” Bajie laughed. “If Master becomes a Buddha, I too hope to become one. Why would I covet wealth and honor? You damned hulking oaf! Wait here for me. Once the scriptures are delivered, I shall come back and return with you.” The fool shouldered the load, Sha Monk led the horse, and the Pilgrim guided the Holy Monk; together they lowered their cloud and landed beside the Scripture-Watching Tower.

p.src: Taizong and all his officials saw them together. He immediately descended the tower to welcome them, saying, “Has my imperial brother returned?” The Tang Monk at once prostrated himself. Taizong helped him up and asked, “Who are these three?” The Tang Monk replied, “They are disciples I took on during the journey.” Taizong was delighted and ordered his attendants, “Saddle my imperial horse and invite my imperial brother to mount it and return to court with me.” The Tang Monk thanked him for the favor and mounted. The Great Sage followed close behind, brandishing his gold-banded cudgel, while Bajie and Sha Monk supported the horse and carried the load; following the imperial procession, they all entered Chang’an. Truly it was a sight such as this:

p.src: Now the monks young and old at Hongfu Temple in Chang’an, where the Tang Monk had formerly lived, saw that the crowns of several pine trees had all turned eastward, and exclaimed in astonishment, “How strange! How very strange! There was no wind last night, so why have all the treetops twisted around?” Among them was a former disciple of Tripitaka, who said, “Quickly, bring my robes! Our old master who went for the scriptures has returned.” The monks asked, “How do you know?” The former disciple replied, “When Master left, he said, ‘After I am gone, whether three or five years pass, or six or seven, whenever you see the tips of the pine branches pointing east, I shall be returning.’ My master’s words are the holy utterance of a Buddha, and that is how I know.” They hastily put on their robes and went out. By the time they reached the western street, word had already spread: “The scripture pilgrims have just arrived, and His Majesty has escorted them into the city.” Hearing this, the monks hurried forward and soon encountered the procession. On seeing the imperial procession, they dared not approach, but followed behind as far as the palace gate.

p.src: The Tang Monk dismounted and entered the court with the others. He left the dragon-horse and the scripture bundles with the Pilgrim, Bajie, and Sha Monk, who stood below the jade steps. Taizong summoned his imperial brother into the hall and granted him a seat. The Tang Monk again gave thanks and sat, then asked that the scripture scrolls be carried in. The Pilgrim and the others brought them out, and the attendants passed them up. Taizong asked further, “How many scriptures are there? And how did you obtain them?” Tripitaka replied, “This monk, your servant, reached Spirit Mountain and paid homage to the Buddha. At his command the two Venerable Ones, Ananda and Kasyapa, first led us to the precious tower and gave us a vegetarian meal, then took us to the jeweled pavilion to transmit the scriptures. The Venerable Ones demanded a gift. Since we had prepared none and gave them nothing, they handed us the scriptures as they were. After thanking the Buddha for his grace, we set out eastward, but a demonic wind suddenly snatched the scriptures away. Fortunately, my young disciples possess some magic powers and chased them down, but the scrolls were all thrown about and scattered. When we unrolled them to inspect them, they proved to be blank copies without a single character. Greatly alarmed, we returned to report the matter and plead for the true scriptures. The Buddha said: When these scriptures were completed, a holy monk once took them down the mountain and recited them at the house of Elder Zhao in the kingdom of Sravasti, ensuring safety for the living of his household and deliverance for the dead. He charged only three pecks and three pints of gold in rice grains, and I thought even that too cheap; his descendants later had no money to spend. We understood that the Buddha knew perfectly well of the two Venerable Ones’ demand, so we had no choice but to give them the imperial purple-gold alms bowl. Only then did they transmit the true scriptures bearing written words. The canon comprises thirty-five divisions. We selected several scrolls from each and brought back a total of five thousand and forty-eight scrolls. That number constitutes one complete canon.”

p.src: Taizong was more delighted than ever and ordered, “Have the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepare a banquet in the eastern pavilion as our thanks.” Then he noticed the three disciples standing below the steps, all extraordinary in appearance, and asked, “Are your worthy disciples truly foreigners?” The elder prostrated himself and replied, “My first disciple’s surname is Sun and his religious name is Wukong; I also call him Pilgrim Sun. He comes from the Water-Curtain Cave on Flower-Fruit Mountain in the kingdom of Aolai, in the Eastern Continent of Superior Body. Five hundred years ago he caused havoc in Heaven and was imprisoned by the Buddha in a stone casket beneath Five Elements Mountain, at the border of the Western Region. Bodhisattva Guanyin urged him toward goodness, and he willingly took refuge in the faith. I released him when I reached that place, and throughout the journey I owed a great deal of my protection to this disciple. My second disciple’s surname is Zhu and his religious name is Wuneng; I also call him Zhu Bajie. He comes from Cloud-Road Cave on Mount Fuling. He was causing trouble at Gao Family Village in Tibet when the Bodhisattva likewise urged him toward goodness, and it was thanks to the Pilgrim that he was subdued and accepted. Along the road his strength was valuable in carrying the load, and he rendered service when we crossed the waters. My third disciple’s surname is Sha and his religious name is Wujing; I also call him Monk Sha. He was originally a monster haunting the River of Flowing Sands. He too was urged toward goodness by the Bodhisattva and now observes the Buddhist teaching as a monk. As for that horse, it is not the one Your Majesty bestowed upon me.” Taizong said, “Its coat and markings are the same. How can it not be?” Tripitaka replied, “When I reached Eagle-Grief Stream on Coiled-Snake Mountain and was crossing the water, my original horse was swallowed by this one. Fortunately, the Pilgrim summoned the Bodhisattva and asked about this horse’s origins. It proved to be a son of the Dragon King of the Western Sea who had committed an offense; the Bodhisattva had also delivered him and instructed him to serve as my mount. At that time he transformed himself into the original horse, with exactly the same coat and markings. Thanks to him we crossed mountains and ridges and traversed rugged country: I rode him on the outward journey, and he bore the scriptures on our return. We have relied greatly upon his strength as well.”

p.src: When Taizong heard this, he praised them without end. Then he asked, “On your long journey to the West, exactly how great a distance did you travel?” Tripitaka replied, “As I recall the Bodhisattva’s words, it was a full hundred and eight thousand li. Along the way I kept no reckoning of the distance; I know only that fourteen cycles of winter and summer passed. Every day brought mountains, and every day brought ridges. Every forest we met was vast, and every river broad and mighty. We also passed through the realms of several kings, and all their seals are here for verification.” He called, “Disciples, bring up the travel passport and submit it to His Majesty.” It was handed up at once. Taizong examined it and saw that it had been issued three days before the full moon of the ninth month in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan. Taizong laughed and said, “You have labored long on this distant journey; it is now already the twenty-seventh year of Zhenguan.” The document bore the seals of the kingdoms of Precious Image, Black Rooster, Cart-Slow, Western Liang Women, Sacrifice, Scarlet-Purple, Bhiksu, Dharma-Destroying, and India, as well as the seals of Fengxian Commandery, Yuhua Prefecture, and Jinping Prefecture. When Taizong had finished examining it, he put it away.

p.src: That evening, when darkness fell, the banquet of thanksgiving ended. Taizong returned to the palace, and all the officials went home. The Tang Monk and his companions returned to Hongfu Monastery, where they found the monks bowing to the ground to welcome them. Just as they entered the monastery gate, the monks reported, “Master, early this morning all the treetops suddenly leaned toward the east. We remembered what you had said, so we went out of the city to meet you, and sure enough, you had arrived.” The elder was overjoyed and entered the abbot’s quarters. This time Bajie neither clamored for tea and food nor made a noisy commotion; Pilgrim and Friar Sand were each calm and dignified. Because they had attained the fruition of the Way, they were naturally serene. That night they slept.

p.src: When it had been written, the holy monk was summoned at once. The elder was already waiting outside the court gate to offer thanks. Hearing the summons, he hurried inside and prostrated himself. Taizong had him invited up into the hall and handed him the composition. After reading it from beginning to end, the elder descended once more to give thanks and memorialized, “Your Majesty’s language is lofty and antique, its principles and meaning profound and subtle. But I do not know what title it bears.” Taizong replied, “I composed it orally during the night to express my thanks to my imperial brother. I have entitled it ‘Preface to the Sacred Teaching.’ I do not know whether it is any good.” The elder kowtowed and thanked him over and over. Taizong continued, “My talent is unworthy of fine jade, and my words are ashamed before inscriptions of bronze and stone. As for the Buddhist canon, I am especially unlearned in it. This preface, extemporized aloud, is truly crude and clumsy. My sullied brush has defaced tablets of gold, and I have set rubble on display in a grove of pearls. When I examine myself and reflect upon it, my face reddens and my heart is ashamed. It is hardly worthy of praise; your thanks are quite undeserved.”

p.src: At this, all the officials offered their congratulations together, reverently bowed before the imperial composition on the Sacred Teaching, and circulated it throughout the court and beyond. Taizong said, “How would it be if my imperial brother expounded and recited the true scriptures for us?” The elder replied, “Your Majesty, if the true scriptures are to be expounded, we must find a Buddhist sanctuary. The imperial hall is not a place where they may be recited.” Taizong was delighted and immediately asked the attending officials, “Which monastery within the city of Chang’an is pure and clean?” The Grand Academician Xiao Yu stepped out from the ranks and memorialized, “Within the city there is a clean monastery called Wild Goose Pagoda Monastery.” Taizong immediately ordered the officials, “Each of you reverently carry several scrolls of the true scriptures and accompany me to Wild Goose Pagoda Monastery, where we shall invite my imperial brother to discourse upon them.”

p.src: Each of the officials accordingly took up some scrolls and followed Taizong’s imperial procession to the monastery, where a high platform was erected and everything arranged in perfect order. The elder then instructed, “Bajie and Friar Sand, lead the dragon-horse and put the luggage in order; Pilgrim, remain by my side.” Then he said to Taizong, “Your Majesty, if you wish the true scriptures to spread throughout the world, copies must be transcribed before they can be distributed. The originals should be treasured and preserved, never treated with careless irreverence.” Taizong laughed again and said, “My imperial brother’s words are most fitting, most fitting indeed.” He thereupon summoned officials of the Hanlin Academy and the Secretariat to transcribe the true scriptures. He also founded a monastery east of the city and named it Scripture-Copying Monastery.

Then he said to Taizong, “Your Majesty, if you wish the true scriptures to spread throughout the world, copies must be transcribed before they can be distributed.
The originals should be treasured and preserved, never treated with careless irreverence.”
Taizong laughed again and said, “My imperial brother’s words are most fitting, most fitting indeed.”
He thereupon summoned officials of the Hanlin Academy and the Secretariat to transcribe the true scriptures.
He also founded a monastery east of the city and named it Scripture-Copying Monastery.

p.src: The elder carried several scrolls onto the platform and was just about to chant them when suddenly a fragrant wind began to coil around them. The Eight Great Vajra Guardians appeared in midair and cried aloud, “You who would recite the scriptures, put down the scrolls and follow us back to the West!” Below, Pilgrim and the other two disciples, together with the white horse, rose straight up from level ground; the elder too cast down the scripture scrolls, rose from the platform into the ninth heaven, and soared away through the air after them. Taizong and all the officials were so startled that they bowed toward the sky. Indeed:

p.src: When Taizong and the officials had finished bowing, he selected eminent monks and had a grand Water-and-Land Dharma Assembly held there in Wild Goose Pagoda Monastery. They read and chanted the true scriptures of the Great Canon, delivering the tormented ghosts of the netherworld and bestowing blessings universally. The transcribed scriptures were then spread throughout the realm, but of that no more need be said.

p.src: Now the Eight Great Vajra Guardians rode upon a fragrant wind, leading the elder and his four companions—the horse making five—and returned to Vulture Peak. Their journey there and back had taken exactly eight days. At that time, all the divine beings of Vulture Peak were listening to the Buddha preach. The Eight Vajra Guardians led master and disciples inside and addressed the Tathagata: “Your disciples previously received the golden decree to escort the holy monk and his companions to the Tang realm. We delivered the scriptures, and have now returned especially to report the fulfillment of your command.” The Tang Monk and the others were then summoned forward to receive their appointments. The Tathagata said, “Holy monk, in your former life you were originally my second disciple, named Golden Cicada. Because you would not heed the Dharma and treated my great teaching with contempt, I banished your true spirit and caused you to be reborn in the Eastern Land. Now I rejoice that you have taken refuge, upheld my blessing, and followed my teaching to obtain the true scriptures. Your merit is exceedingly great. I therefore raise you to a high office and true fruition, and name you the Buddha of Candana Merit. —Sun Wukong, because you caused havoc in the Celestial Palace, I used my profound powers to confine you beneath Five Elements Mountain. Happily, when the term of your heavenly punishment was fulfilled, you entered the Buddhist faith; and I rejoice that you concealed your faults and exalted what was good, earning merit by subduing demons and monsters along the road and carrying your task through from beginning to end. I therefore raise you to a high office and true fruition, and name you the Victorious Fighting Buddha. —Zhu Wuneng, you were once Marshal Tianpeng, a water deity of the Celestial River. Because you became drunk at the Peach Banquet and molested a celestial maiden, you were banished to the lower world and reborn with the body of a beast. Fortunately, you retained an attachment to human form. Though you committed sins at Cloudy Paths Cave on Mount Fuling, it is pleasing that you embraced the great teaching, entered my Buddhist order, and protected the holy monk on his journey. Yet you remained stubborn, and your lust was not extinguished. Because you earned merit by carrying the luggage, I raise you to true fruition and appoint you Cleanser of the Altars.” Bajie cried out, “They have all become Buddhas! Why have you made me merely a Cleanser of the Altars?” The Tathagata replied, “Because your appetite is hearty, your body indolent, and your belly capacious. Throughout the world’s four great continents, many people revere my teaching. At every Buddhist ceremony, you shall cleanse the altar by consuming its offerings. It is a rank with ample benefits—how can it be bad?” —Sha Wujing, you were formerly the Curtain-Raising General. Because you shattered a crystal goblet at the Peach Banquet, you were banished to the lower world. You fell into the Flowing Sands River, where you destroyed lives, ate human flesh, and accumulated sin. Happily, you took refuge in my teaching, sincerely and reverently upheld my blessing, protected the holy monk, and earned merit by climbing mountains and leading the horse. I therefore raise you to a high office and true fruition, and name you the Golden-Bodied Arhat.” Then he called to the white horse: “You were originally a son of the Dragon King Guangjin of the Western Ocean. Because you defied your father’s command, you committed the sin of unfilial conduct. Fortunately, you took refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and my order. Day after day you bore the holy monk westward, and then carried the sacred scriptures eastward. You too have earned merit. I therefore raise you to true fruition and name you the Heavenly Dragon Horse of the Eight Classes.”

p.src: The elder and his four companions all kowtowed in gratitude for the favor bestowed upon them. The horse also gave thanks. The Jiedi guardian was then ordered to lead the horse down to the Dragon-Transformation Pool beside the rear cliff of Vulture Peak and push it into the water. In an instant, the horse stretched itself and shed its hide; its head and horns were transformed, golden scales sprang over its whole body, and silver whiskers grew beneath its cheeks and chin. Wreathed in an auspicious aura, with propitious clouds beneath its four claws, it flew from the Dragon-Transformation Pool and coiled around the soaring ornamental pillar inside the mountain gate. All the Buddhas praised the Tathagata’s mighty Dharma.

p.src: Pilgrim Sun then said to the Tang Monk, “Master, I have now become a Buddha, the same as you. Surely I cannot still be wearing this golden fillet while you go on reciting that Tight-Fillet Spell to torment me? Quickly recite a Loosening-Fillet Spell, take it off, and smash it to powder, so that whatever bodhisattva it was can never use it to torment anyone else.” The Tang Monk replied, “At the time, I used that means to restrain you only because you were so difficult to control. Now that you have become a Buddha, it has naturally vanished. How could it still remain upon your head? Feel for yourself.” Pilgrim raised a hand and felt his head; sure enough, the fillet was gone.
